Dad takes me to the range and starts my education. (Dad was military and a hunter and had many guns) Hands me a six shooter, we practice until I get very good with it. Can reload and fire very quick, groupings tight. I am proud of myself. Then Dad puts the gun in my other hand and says start all over, because what if your arm or hand is shot and you can't use it. I was a teen in shape, but why? I run and we go to the range. I am out of breath, sweaty and my extremities are a little shaky from the run. He hands me the same gun and says shoot. My shooting sucks. He says that is adrenaline and that is what will be coursing through your body if you are ever in a serious event. After that, I ran before range time and got good at controlling my weapon. I am proud of myself. Then dad hands me a different gun and we start the process all over again. Dad had many tricks up his sleeve as I was going to find out.

It depends, there are variables. Do you want something for close quarters, like inside you house (which is what most people want). If so, you want to start out with a handgun, preferably a 9mm (mostly because 9mm ammo is most readily available and won't break the bank). If you've never learned to shoot, you might feel more comfortable with a six shooter, say a little Smith & Wesson. You could also go with a shotgun. The nice thing about a shotgun is racking in a load is a sound everyone knows and that sound will likely scare someone away without you having to confront them. Another nice thing about a shotgun is you can load the first shell with bird shot, the person will survive but will be hurting and you can load the following shells with buckshot - there's a lot of options. Veteran gun owners will tell you to always shoot to kill, but I do understand killing doesn't sit well with some people, hence the bird shot. There are gun ranges everywhere. If I were you, go to a local gun store and ask them what gun ranges they recommend. Most gun ranges also provide classes for beginners. Once you go through the classes, start going to the range and you will meet people the regulars - ask questions, most people love to help out new people. My biggest recommendation is learn the gun laws in your state and good luck.
